Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. No sign of the sun as it is still pretty overcast at Buffalo Park. Robson Foulkes and Luke Watson are the two openers for New Zealand Under-19. Bashir Ahmad to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

For Afghanistan Under-19, there isn't much to highlight. After winning the toss and choosing to bat first in overcast conditions that favoured the bowlers, Afghanistan appears to have miscalculated the situation at the toss. Losing two early wickets within the first three overs, Jamshid Zadran emerged as the sole batter who showed intent and settled in a bit. His 22 runs off 32 deliveries stand tall on the scorecard, with every other player getting out in single-digit scores, apart from a brief burst by Arab Gul, who contributed 10 runs. Afghanistan now finds themselves in a challenging position, having dug a hole that they hope for a miracle to climb out of. The batting collapse has left them in a difficult situation, and they will be banking on something extraordinary to turn things around. Will we witness a twist in the tale, or will the second innings be a straightforward task for the Kiwis? Let's wait as the second innings unfolds in a bit.

Matt Rowe, the man of the moment is down for a chat and just cannot stop smiling. He says that the ball was swinging around and it seemed like a good toss to lose. He further says he is pretty happy as the ball came nicely off his hands in this game. Ends by saying that small totals are tricky but the boys have 50 overs in hand and should be able to get things done.

The New Zealand Under-19 bowlers have showcased a dominant performance, and will now be itching to quickly wrap up this game with the bat. Ryan Tsourgas set the tone by taking the wicket of opener Hassan Eisakhil in the very first over, putting Afghanistan Under-19 on the back foot. Khalid Taniwal's brief stay at the crease was also cut short by Ryan in his second over. Despite a fleeting period of resistance by the Afghanistan batters, Matt Rowe took center stage and dismantled the middle order effortlessly. Delivering a top-notch performance, Rowe bowled an exceptional delivery to breach the defence of Sohail Khan Zurmati and subsequently claim the crucial wicket of Jamshid Zadran, who was looking settled. Rowe continued his extended spell and secured a five-wicket haul by dismissing Rahimullah Zurmati and Numan Shah. Ewald Schreuder and the skipper Oscar Jackson then joined the bowling attack to swiftly wrap up the tail.

A scintillating bowling display from the Kiwis! They felt at home with these overcast conditions and their pacers took full advantage of it. They have bowled out the Afgahns for their second-lowest total in the ICC Under-19 World Cup history. Matt Rowe led from the front with a stunning five-wicket haul and finds himself among big names like Trent Boult and Tim Southee for the best figures for New Zealand Under-19 at this level.

We are moments away from the start of the match but before that, the players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Afghanistan's first followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

PITCH REPORT - HD Ackerman is pitchside along with Marina Iqbal. He says it's slightly overcast and the temperature is at 19 degrees with no wind. The humidity is at 77 percent which might help the ball swing a bit. He further mentions that the straight fence is 76 meters and for a right-hander the off-side fence is 64 meters and the on-side is 63 meters. Marina says Afghanistan has taken some gamble here with the overcast conditions. She says the deck is spongy and has grass covered with it that is rolled on well but has a few sweat patches. She further says that the ball will swing and seam and anything bowled shorter will hold on to the surface making things hard for the batters. She then concludes that 230-240 on the board would be a good total to defend with the conditions not changing much throughout the game.

Oscar Jackson, the captain of New Zealand Under-19 says that they would have bowled first anyways. Adds that they will look to take advantage of the overcast conditions and the moisture on it will help their pacers too. Tells that they have not taken DLS into account yet and hopes that rain does not affect much in this game. Says that unfortunately the centurion from te last match, Snehith Reddy misses out due to a slight niggle in the achilles. Informs they have made three changes in total.

Naseer Khan Maroofkhil, the skipper of Afghanistan Under-19 says the wicket looks good to bat and hopefully they will put a good total on the board. He then says that with no wind around he is hopeful that the spinners will do well too. Informs they have made one change to the team.

New Zealand Under-19 (Playing XI) - Luke Watson, Robson Foulkes (In place of Snehith Reddy), Tom Jones, Ollie Tewatiya, Oscar Jackson (C), Lachlan Stackpole, Zac Cumming, Sam Clode (WK) (In place of Alex Thompson), Matt Rowe, Ewald Schreuder, Ryan Tsourgas (In place of Mason Clarke).

Afghanistan Under-19 (Playing XI) - Naseer Khan Maroofkhil (C), Numan Shah (WK), Hassan Eisakhil, Khalid Taniwal (In place of Wafiullah Tarakhil), Sohail Khan Zurmati, Rahimullah Zurmati, Jamshid Zadran, Arab Gul, Allah Mohammad, Khalil Ahmed, Bashir Ahmad.
TOSS - Afghanistan Under-19 have won the toss and elected to BAT first.

On the flip side, Afghanistan Under-19, led by Naseer Khan Maroofkhil, enter this match following a loss against Pakistan Under-19. Despite a fairly decent outing with the ball, a challenging start with the bat in the previous game has put Afghanistan on the back foot coming into this crucial encounter. Khalil Ahmed who emerged as the standout bowler, well-supported by Bashir Ahmad, Allah Mohammad and skipper Naseer Khan Maroofkhil will have to repeat their performances here. The top order will be under scrutiny after a below-par effort in the previous game, with Sohail Khan Zurmati, Numan Shah and Rahimullah Zurmati getting starts but failing to convert them into substantial innings. Afghanistan will believe they have the talent and capability to turn the tides in their favour and will certainly look to put up a strong performance in this game. Facing the formidable New Zealand Under-19 side, Afghanistan will be eager to rewrite their comeback narrative and potentially upset the form of this Kiwi team. Will they be able to get their first victory or will the Kiwis go past to register their second win? Let's find out as Toss and team news come to you in a bit.

New Zealand Under-19 enter this game with a solid performance and a victorious start against Nepal Under-19. Captain Oscar Jackson, leading from the front, showcased his all-around prowess with both bat and ball in their initial encounter. The momentum and confidence gained in the previous match are poised to bolster the Kiwis in this game. Snehith Reddy has been the standout performer, lighting up the tournament with his unbeaten score of 147 in the first game. Tom Jones and Luke Watson are anticipated to play critical roles with the bat in this game. In the bowling department, Mason Clarke, Ewald Schreuder and Matt Rowe have proven their mettle with top performances in the previous game, forming a formidable bowling unit. With a well-rounded team, New Zealand Under-19 will be aiming to maintain the strong momentum and continue their winning ways in this crucial match.

Greetings and a warm welcome to Match number 11 in the 15th edition of the Men's Under-19 Cricket World Cup, set to unfold at Buffalo Park in East London. The stage is indeed set as New Zealand Under-19 and Afghanistan Under-19 prepare to engage in a crucial match within the group stage which promises to be an entertaining encounter.
... MATCH DAY ...

It is now time for Match number 11 of the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup 2024 and in a Group D clash, New Zealand Under-19 will go up against Afghanistan Under-19 in a crucial clash at Buffalo Park in East London. New Zealand Under-19 made a winning start to their campaign against Nepal Under-19, beating them fairly comfortably by 64 runs whereas Afghanistan Under-19 were surprisingly handed a real thumping by fellow Asian giants Pakistan Under-19. New Zealand Under-19 will be eyeing their second win and keep on gaining momentum ahead of the next stage of the competition and Afghanistan Under-19 will be looking to bounce back quickly and keep their hopes of making it through to the next round alive with a win. For New Zealand Under-19, the top order got off to a decent start before a couple of batters in the middle order took charge. Snehith Reddy hit a big ton and was well-supported by skipper Oscar Jackson. With the ball in hand, Mason Clarke bowled really well and so did a couple of other bowlers and they will be looking to get another win under their belt. As for Afghanistan Under-19, their bowling was decent as Bashir Ahmad and Khalil Ahmed bowled really well but they allowed a few big stands to brew against Pakistan which cost them dearly. The main issue though was with the bat as they were blown away by the opposition bowlers and bundled out for just 103 with only four batters getting in double figures. Can Afghanistan Under-19 spring a comeback and stun the Kiwis? Or will New Zealand Under-19 put on another strong showing? We shall find out.
